U6.3 · Self & Creativity II — Depth

Read the self in the work

Before technique: look at a piece and ask — was this made while searching openly, or while locking a choice? Can you see the switch?

Open to invent. Focus to finish.

(Tao of Creativity)

U6.3 · Self & Creativity II — Depth

1 · Confidence is practiced

Creative confidence grows from doing — not from waiting to feel gifted.

Belief in your creative capacity lies at the heart of innovation.

(Tao of Creativity — after Kelley & Kelley)

Image: Pen-and-ink sheet by Leonardo da Vinci with two studies of the Virgin holding the Christ Child and a cat, and three smaller studies of the Child with the cat, each pose tried differently.

Two studies of the Virgin and Child with a cat and three studies of the Child with a cat · Leonardo da Vinci · Public domain · Source

Aligns with U6 idea 1. Kelley wording taught as course paraphrase until page pin in lesson refs if needed.

U6.3 · Self & Creativity II — Depth

2 · Can I? Should I?

Agency needs confidence and centrality — belief you can and that it matters who you are.

Two gates: Can I act creatively here? Should I spend creative effort on this?

(Tao of Creativity — after Beghetto & Karwowski)

Image: Notebook page with two pencil sketches of possible phonograph designs, dated 29 November 1877 and signed by Edison, Charles Batchelor, and John Kruesi; the lower design is the one the National Park Service says was assigned to Kruesi to build.

Phonograph drawings, 29 November 1877 · Thomas A. Edison (drawing; Thomas Edison National Historical Park, National Park Service) · Public domain · Source

U6.3 · Self & Creativity II — Depth

3 · Habits outlast the high

Personal creativity redesigns everyday psychic energy — dress, work, relations under briefs.

Personal creativity consists in changing the domain of personal life.

(Csikszentmihalyi 1996)

Image: Black-and-white photograph of a large drafting room with rows of tables.

Drafting room, Navy Dept. LCCN2016873947 · Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Source

U6.3 · Self & Creativity II — Depth

4 · Focus is not magic selection

Why: the study predicted focused-attention would help convergent thinking — it did not hold up. What then: use FA to return to one object when you already have options; do not expect it to invent the right pick for you.

FA meditation did not sustain convergent thinking as predicted.

(Tao of Creativity — after Colzato et al. 2012)

Image: The Wright brothers' 1902 biplane glider in flight over the Kitty Hawk dunes, its pilot on the lower wing, under a cloudy sky.

Gliding flight, Wright Glider, Kitty Hawk, NC, 1902 · Wilbur and Orville Wright · Public domain · Source

Why/what-then: students must not leave thinking FA = automatic good picks. Convergent work still needs criteria, comparison, and craft — attention style is only one tool.

U6.3 · Self & Creativity II — Depth

5 · Imaginal as mediation

The imaginal is a mediating function — neither raw fantasy nor mere sensation.

Active imagination is the mirror par excellence… the imaginative function is truly central, mediating.

(Corbin 1972, 7)

Image: Leonardo sketch of a flying machine from around 1505.

Leonardo Design for a Flying Machine, c. 1505 · Leonardo da Vinci · Public domain · Source

Recycled from the author’s dissertation quotations for classroom schemata.

U6.3 · Self & Creativity II — Depth

6 · Dose honesty + Opt-out

Opt-out means: you may skip the embodied warm-up — sit quietly or jump to listing — no explanation. Dose honesty means: the lab used ~35 minutes; our classroom version is shorter and untested — never pretend the minutes match.

Adaptation is allowed. Pretending the minutes match is not.

(Tao of Creativity)

Image: A printed 1911 table of Binet–Simon test results from two Paris schools: rows of test tasks cross-referenced with pass rates (out of 10) for each age group.

Tableau de résultats au test de Binet-Simon · Alfred Binet · Public domain · Source

Define Opt-out on the slide for teenagers. Lab card repeats it. Consent before technique.

U6.3 · Self & Creativity II — Depth

Recall check

Alone, from memory, 3 minutes.

  1. What grows creative confidence?
  2. Name the two agency gates.
  3. What does personal creativity redesign?
  4. What is the imaginal’s job?
  5. What does Castoriadis say method is?

Course geometric background · threshold · #7a624a21 · Original course SVG

Answers:

1. Practiced action / doing creative work.

2. Can I? Should I?

3. Everyday habits / personal life domain.

4. Mediating function between banal dualisms.

5. The operating set of categories (p. 11).

Exercise 1 · Shared-image note

Name one image in your brief that feels larger than you — brand, myth, meme, style. Write how you will host or refuse it.

Shared image + host/refuse sentence.

List three categories your brief assumes (user, luxury, sustainable…). Star one you will revise.

Three categories + one starred revision.
